field_labels.ССЕЕ_mw: net battery signal (derived, resynced after the fix)

description: New failure mode (not solar/load -- battery charge/discharge specifically). Both batt_charge_mw and batt_discharge_mw got stuck through the entire evening peak and overnight period: 1.9/2497.9 MW from 17:40:36Z (22 polls), then 3.8/1758.3 MW through 2026-09-28T05:00:44Z (111 more polls, ~9.25h) -- 133 polls total, ~11.3 hours frozen without a single change. Confirmed both by direct inspection of raw records and visually on the live dashboard (flat ССЕЕ зареждане/разреждане lines through the whole overnight window). Recovered in a single poll at 2026-09-28T05:05:03Z. ADDENDUM (found later same session): wind generation (ВяЕЦ) was frozen in the exact same window too, in two stuck sub-values: 368.96 MW from 17:40:36Z to 19:35:34Z, then jumped to 450.75 MW and stayed stuck there through 2026-09-28T05:00:44Z. Confirmed by scanning for consecutive-identical ВяЕЦ values across the window; recovered at the same 05:05:03Z boundary as the battery fields. SECOND ADDENDUM (found later same session, after user re-flagged the morning discharge as still looking wrong): the recovery boundary at 05:05:03Z was NOT a clean return to trustworthy data. The feed jumped from a corrected 1087 MW to a raw 1797 MW discharge in a single poll, then lingered at 700-1700 MW through ~06:00 -- roughly 1.5-2x higher and decaying far slower than ENTSOE's actual hourly data for the same hours (1099.6 MW at 05:00, 93.8 MW at 06:00, 0.3 MW at 07:00).
correction_method: TWO ATTEMPTS -- the first was wrong and had to be reverted, worth recording why. Attempt 1 used the standard playbook method (prior-day shape, ratio-blended between boundaries) and looked locally smooth, but the user caught that it implied ~16 GWh of discharge with almost no charging over the window -- not physically sustainable for the actual BESS fleet, and a bad case of the same ratio-blow-up risk logged in the 2026-09-14 entry below (the recovery boundary's reference denominator was small, inflating the ratio, then that ratio got applied across the evening-peak portion of the window where magnitudes were much larger -- produced a false 9006 MW discharge record). Reverted via `git revert` (commit was already pushed). Attempt 2 (kept): fetched actual ENTSOE-published generation data for BG via energy-charts.info (`energy_charts.py`, public_power/bg, fields 'Battery' = discharge, 'Battery Consumption' = charge) for the corrupted window, linearly interpolated from ENTSOE's native hourly resolution to the dashboard's 5-min resolution, and wrote those interpolated values directly into the corrupted records (no scaling/blending against a neighboring day at all). This revealed the true shape ESO's own SCADA feed hid: discharge taper from ~1850 MW at 16:00 UTC down to near-zero by 22:00, then the battery CHARGES overnight (peaking ~620 MW charge around 00:00 UTC) rather than continuing to discharge, then discharge ramps back up toward dawn -- the opposite of attempt 1's monotonic-taper assumption. Resulting window energy: 6.06 GWh discharged vs 1.78 GWh charged, a plausible net (evening-peak-heavy) balance. records.json/records_history.json regenerated -- batt_dis record correctly stayed at the real 4020.5 MW (an unrelated, uncorrected evening-peak poll on 09-28), not the false 9006 MW from attempt 1. WIND FIX (same session, same method as attempt 2): fetched ENTSOE's 'Wind onshore' series for BG via energy_charts.py for 2026-09-27/28, linearly interpolated from hourly to 5-min resolution, and wrote those values into ВяЕЦ for every record in the same 17:40:36Z-05:05:03Z window (133 records, same as the battery fix). ENTSOE showed wind actually varying smoothly through the window (374->488 MW evening peak at 20:00, dropping to ~293 MW at 21:00, then a slow ~300-326 MW plateau overnight, declining after 05:00) -- nothing like the two flat stuck values SCADA reported. records.json/records_history.json regenerated; no wind record type is tracked there so no anomaly check needed. MORNING WINDOW EXTENSION (same session, same ENTSOE-interpolation method): extended the corrected window from 05:05:03Z through 07:00:08Z (23 more records), replacing batt_charge_mw/batt_discharge_mw/ССЕЕ_mw with ENTSOE Battery/Battery Consumption interpolated to 5-min resolution, same as the main fix. Produces a smooth monotonic taper (1015 MW discharge at 05:05 down to 8 MW by 06:55, charge ramping continuously 0->903 MW) instead of the raw feed's erratic post-recovery jump and slow decay. records.json regenerated; no new record-break (max discharge in this window ~1087 MW, well under the real 4020.5 MW record).
note: Lesson: for battery charge/discharge specifically, ENTSOE's own actual-generation data (via energy-charts.info) directly reports a 'Battery'/'Battery Consumption' series for BG -- prefer fetching that as ground truth over inferring from a neighboring day's SCADA shape, since battery dispatch is a scheduled/economic decision (charge when cheap, discharge when expensive) that doesn't reliably repeat night-to-night the way solar's weather-driven curve roughly does. Also: while investigating, discovered this session's own earlier `git revert` + push to the shared `data` branch caused the VPS poller's git sync to silently fail for ~2 hours (auto-rebase conflicts swallowed by push_data.sh's `|| true` fallback) -- it kept fetching and committing locally the whole time (fetch itself was never broken) but stopped pushing to GitHub. Fixed by SSHing in and running `git rebase --abort` + `git pull --rebase origin data` + `git push origin data` by hand; resolved cleanly. Direct pushes to the shared data branch while the VPS cron is also writing to it are a real conflict risk -- worth rebasing/pushing quickly and double-checking the VPS's git sync afterward whenever this happens. Also found: the SAME frozen window affected wind (ВяЕЦ) as well as battery, not just battery alone -- when a SCADA freeze is found, check ALL fields for the same time range, not just the one the user first flagged. ENTSOE's 'Wind onshore' series (energy_charts.py, public_power/bg) is a good ground-truth substitute for wind too, same as it was for battery. Also: don't trust the SCADA feed's own 'recovery' timestamp at face value -- after a freeze, the feed can come back with a miscalibrated/biased reading for a while before it actually re-syncs with reality. Always cross-check a chunk of data AFTER the nominal recovery point against ENTSOE too, not just the frozen window itself.

field_labels.gen_total_mw: sum of 9 gen sources (derived, resummed after ФЕЦ fix)

description: Fifth occurrence of the same failure mode (prior: 2026-08-18, 2026-08-19, 2026-08-25, 2026-08-26). Load climbed steadily from a normal ~1.07x ratio vs the prior day up to 1.49x (peak 5843.6 MW at 15:20:03Z, second-highest ever recorded for this field). Solar failed to taper toward sunset -- still 2741 MW at 18:20 Sofia local (15:20 UTC) vs 942 MW the day before at the same local time (2.6x ratio), instead of the normal sunset decline. All other generation sources (nuclear, coal, hydro, wind, biomass) and cross-border flows tracked the prior day's normal variation throughout, unaffected -- confirms the corruption was isolated to just these two fields, not a whole-feed outage. Both snapped instantly back to a ~1.0-1.07x ratio in the same single poll at 2026-09-14T15:25:03Z (18:25 Sofia local).
correction_method: Same method as prior occurrences: interpolated from 2026-09-13's shape at matching times-of-day (nearest BG-local minute-of-day match), per-field scale factors blended linearly between the boundary ratios measured at the last clean record (13:45 Sofia local, load 1.075x / solar 1.424x) and the first recovered record (18:25 Sofia local, load 1.069x / solar 1.017x). load_mw synced alongside Товар на РБ; gen_total_mw resummed from the 9 corrected gen-source fields (only ФЕЦ among them changed). Original values preserved per-record under _raw_backup. records.json/records_history.json regenerated afterward -- no false peak_consumption/export/peak_gen records were set from the corrupted window.
note: Cleanest recovery boundary of the five occurrences so far -- solar snapped to within 1.7% of the prior day's value at the exact same local time, and load to within 6.9%, both in a single 5-min poll.

description: Fourth occurrence of the same failure mode (1st: 2026-08-18 afternoon, 2nd: 2026-08-19 predawn, 3rd: 2026-08-25 afternoon). Solar jumped instantly from 0 to 2084 MW at 03:05:04Z (still dark -- 06:05 Sofia local, real sunrise the day before didn't reach that level until ~06:20) then plateaued/drifted 2084-2812 MW instead of a real sunrise ramp; load jumped from 3274 to 5410 MW (1.65x) at the same instant. Both dropped toward normal-looking values at 2026-08-26T06:35:03Z.
correction_method: Same method as the prior three: interpolated from 2026-08-25's shape at matching times-of-day, per-field scale factors blended between boundary ratios (load 1.010x->0.974x, solar assumed 1.0x->0.664x -- yesterday's solar was ~0 at the start anchor so no meaningful start ratio to measure). load_mw synced alongside Товар на РБ. Original values preserved per-record under _raw_backup.
note: Recovery was less clean-cut than the prior three occurrences (no exact instant snap-back to a stable value -- 06:35-06:50 UTC values are plausible but not an obviously perfect match to the prior day, this was the closest reasonable boundary given data ends at 06:50 as of this fix). Worth a follow-up check once more of today's data has landed. Four occurrences now -- strongly recurring ESO-side pattern.

description: Third occurrence of the same failure mode as 2026-08-18 and 2026-08-19: load climbed steadily from a normal ~0.99x ratio vs the prior day up to 1.44x (peak 6569 MW, again far above this project's ~4600 MW historical ceiling), and solar failed to taper -- still 2283 MW at 20:15 Sofia local (17:15 UTC), a 5.6x ratio vs the same time the day before. Both snapped back simultaneously at 2026-08-25T17:20:03Z.
correction_method: Same method as the two prior occurrences: interpolated from 2026-08-24's shape at matching times-of-day, with per-field scale factors blended between the boundary ratios (load 0.985x->1.032x, solar 1.411x->1.0x) for continuity at both ends. load_mw synced alongside Товар на РБ from the start this time (see the load_mw lesson learned on the 2026-08-18 entry). Original values preserved per-record under _raw_backup.
note: Self-corrected on ESO's side at 17:20:03Z, same recovery-time pattern as 2026-08-18 (17:20:03Z) and 2026-08-19 (06:05:03Z -- different clock time, but also a :X0:03Z / :X5:03Z-ish boundary). This is now the third confirmed occurrence -- worth treating as a recurring ESO-side pattern rather than a one-off, though no automatic detection is running per the user's earlier explicit request to keep this manual.

description: Same failure mode as 2026-08-18: load jumped ~85% (3167->5920 MW) and solar appeared at 2541 MW well before sunrise (03:05 UTC = 06:05 Sofia local -- astronomically impossible), both correcting simultaneously at 2026-08-19T06:05:03Z.
correction_method: Copied 2026-08-18's shape at the same times-of-day, scaled by a blend of the boundary ratios (~1.0x at the 03:00 start anchor for both fields, ~1.04x load / ~0.63x solar at the 06:05 recovery anchor) for continuity. Also synced load_mw (the field index.html actually reads, separate from the raw Товар на РБ field) to match -- see the load_mw lesson learned on the 2026-08-18 entry below. Original values preserved per-record under _raw_backup.
note: Self-corrected on ESO's side at 06:05:03Z; fix applied once, load_mw synced this time from the start.

description: ESO's own raw feed (verified via raw_gen_api) froze the battery-charging figure at a single value for 3h50m+, unchanging across every 5-min poll regardless of actual battery state (state flipped between charging/discharging normally throughout, discharge figure kept updating normally). Not a scraper/parsing bug -- ESO's page itself was stuck.
correction_method: Manual one-off fix: zeroed all records where batt_charge_mw exactly matched the frozen value while ССЕЕ_state=discharging. Original value preserved per-record under _raw_backup.batt_charge_mw, each fixed record flagged with _data_corrected=true and _correction_note.
note: An automatic poller-side detection patch (fetch.py) was written and deployed, then reverted at the user's request -- this is a manual, one-time fix for today's occurrence only, not an ongoing safeguard. If this recurs on a future day, it will need to be re-fixed by hand.

description: Solar failed to taper toward sunset (still 2689 MW at 20:15 Sofia local, vs ~140 MW the day before at the same local time) and load climbed to 6612 MW -- no day in this project's dataset has ever recorded BG demand above ~4600 MW. Both snapped back to normal simultaneously at 2026-08-18T17:20:03Z. Confirmed via raw_gen_api that ESO's own page reported these values.
correction_method: Scaled 2026-08-17's shape at the same times-of-day, blending the scale factor from 1.335x (matched to the last known-good ratio before the glitch) down to 1.0x at the 17:20 recovery point, for continuity at both boundaries. ENTSOE was considered and rejected as a correction source: solar has a documented phantom-solar timezone artifact for BG (see compare_eso_dashboard_entsoe.py), and load's ratio vs SCADA wasn't constant, plus ENTSOE had no data yet for the tail of the window. Original values preserved per-record under _raw_backup, each fixed record flagged with _data_corrected=true and _correction_note.
note: This glitch self-corrected on ESO's side at 17:20:03Z; the fix only needed to be applied once.
lesson_learned: Товар на РБ was corrected but the derived load_mw field (set once at fetch time, separate field, what index.html actually reads for its charts/KPIs) was missed -- the dashboard kept showing the bad spike until caught and synced in a follow-up fix. Always sync load_mw alongside Товар на РБ.
